observations: Photo 0: top view of a white games console with a perforated vent grid over half the lid, two wireless controllers lying on it.
Photo 1: front of the console showing a horizontal disc slot on the left, a front USB port at the lower left and the Xbox sphere logo on the power button at the right, so it is a disc model.
Photos 0 to 2: white body, dot-grid vent and slim front match an Xbox One S; the words One S are not printed anywhere in view.
Photos 0 to 2: one white Xbox One style controller with a 3.5mm jack and one blue controller with a share button and hybrid d-pad, the later Series style; the blue pad has blue thumbstick caps.
Photos 0 to 2: no cracks or burn marks visible on the console; light scuffs and dirt on the white controller.
No photo shows the console powered on, a screen, the storage label, the rear ports, the power cable, the HDMI cable, any receipt or any games.
All three photos carry a Jiji dealer watermark (Kingsplen Gaming Gadgets).

read_from: photo 1 Xbox sphere logo on the console front
photos 0 to 2 white dot-grid body and photo 1 disc slot match the One S design; the One S text itself is not read

claims.evidence: Photo 1 Xbox logo and the One S body in photos 0 to 2; the One S is part of the Xbox One family.
Nothing in the photos shows where it was used; the receipt is not shown.
Two controllers are shown in photos 0, 1 and 2.
Both pads carry Xbox buttons, but genuineness cannot be confirmed from photos and the blue one is a later Series style pad, not the one that shipped with this console.
Outside of the console looks clean with no cracks in photos 0 to 2; internal condition is covered by the other claims.

claims.claim: Comes with FC26 package and other games
claims.evidence: No screenshot of the games list and no discs shown; digital games may be tied to the seller's account.
The back and bottom with screws and seals are not shown.
Only shows after long play; no running clip at all.
Rear ports are not shown and nothing is connected.

risks.risk: Console may not power on, or have an HDMI, power supply or overheating fault.
risks.proof: Clip of the console booting to the home screen on a TV with a handwritten code and today's date in shot.
Photo of the bottom label or a screenshot of Settings, System, Storage.

risks.risk: Disc drive may not read or eject discs.
risks.proof: Clip of a disc being inserted, read and ejected.

risks.risk: Controllers may be fakes, have stick drift or fail to pair.
risks.proof: Clip of each controller navigating the menu with both sticks moving.

risks.risk: FC26 and other games may be digital licences on the seller's account, lost on reset.
risks.proof: Screenshot of the games list and the account they belong to, or the discs.

risks.risk: Power and HDMI cables may be missing.
risks.proof: Photo of the power cord and HDMI cable with the console.
risks.if_unproven: as console and pads only, no cables

risks.risk: Console may have been opened, repaired, stolen or banned from online play.
risks.proof: Photo of the back and bottom sticker serial, matching the Settings, System, Console info screen.
risks.if_unproven: as offline only, flagged for serial check

proof_requests: Clip of the console booting to the home screen with a handwritten code and today's date in shot.
Screenshot of Settings, System, Storage, or the bottom label.
Photo of the bottom sticker serial and the Console info screen.
Clip of a disc being read and each controller moving through the menu.
Screenshot of the installed games list showing FC26 and the account.
Photo of the rear ports, the power and HDMI cables, and the UK receipt.
response.reason: The Xbox logo and the white One S body with a disc slot are visible, so it can be priced as an Xbox One S with two pads at worst case: not working, 500GB, no games. A boot clip, storage screen and games list would raise it.
